questions.def: When 'neither/nor' connects singular and plural, agree with the closest.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ happy with the results.

questions.def: Committee acts plural when members act individually.
questions.question: The committee ___ divided in their opinion.

questions.def: Politics (as a topic) is singular, even though it looks plural.
questions.question: Politics ___ often a controversial topic.

questions.def: 'A number of' takes a plural verb.
questions.question: A number of people ___ injured in the accident.

questions.def: Data can be plural or singular, context matters here 'collected' is best.
questions.question: The data ___ collected last year is now outdated.

questions.def: Diseases ending in -s (measles, mumps) usually take singular verbs.
questions.question: Measles ___ a contagious disease.

questions.def: Amounts of money are usually treated as singular.
questions.question: Fifty dollars ___ too much to pay for that shirt.

questions.def: 'Everyone' is singular, so it takes a singular verb.
questions.question: Everyone ___ to bring their own lunch.

questions.def: The verb agrees with the subject 'problem', not 'there'.
questions.question: There ___ to be a problem with the connection.

questions.def: Team acts as one unit, so singular form.
questions.question: The team ___ celebrating their victory.

questions.def: Statistics as a subject is treated as singular.
questions.question: Statistics ___ my weakest subject.

questions.def: News is treated as singular, even though it looks plural.
questions.question: The news ___ surprising.

questions.def: The verb agrees with the plural 'reasons'.
questions.question: What ___ the main reasons for the delay?

questions.def: 'Either/or' agrees with the noun/pronoun closest to the verb.
questions.question: Either John or Mary ___ going to pick you up.

questions.def: The United States is a singular entity, despite the plural name.
questions.question: The United States ___ a large country.

questions.def: All of the (uncountable noun) takes singular verb.
questions.question: All of the cake ___ gone.

questions.def: None can be singular or plural; 'food' is uncountable, therefore singular.
questions.question: None of the food ___ fresh.

questions.def: Effects is plural, so the verb should be plural as well.
questions.question: The effects of climate change ___ obvious.

questions.def: Many a + singular noun takes a singular verb.
questions.question: Many a student ___ felt that way.

questions.def: More than one + singular noun takes a singular verb.
questions.question: More than one student ___ the exam.

questions.def: Costs is plural so we use affect (without 's').
questions.question: The rising costs ___ many families.

questions.def: Half of the (countable plural noun) takes a plural verb.
questions.question: Half of the apples ___ rotten.

questions.def: Family is considered as one unit, use singular verb.
questions.question: My family ___ decided to move.

questions.def: When 'neither/nor' connect singular nouns, the verb agrees with the closest one.
questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ___ happy with the results.

questions.def: When 'the number' is the subject, it is singular; use 'is'.
questions.question: The number of applicants ___ steadily increasing.

questions.def: Jury is treated as a single unit here, so the verb is singular.
questions.question: The jury ___ still deliberating.

questions.def: Subjects like 'economics' are singular despite the 's'.
questions.question: Economics ___ a very demanding subject.

questions.def: With uncountable nouns like cake, 'a lot' is singular.
questions.question: A lot of the cake ___ eaten.

questions.def: 'News' is singular, so the verb is in singular past form.
questions.question: The news ___ everyone deeply.

questions.def: 'Many a' is followed by a singular noun and singular verb.
questions.question: Many a student ___ felt overwhelmed by the workload.
